stays for one release only.

Use pause_keywords and enable_keywords instead; this tool does both and
stays for one release only.

history, so it can be turned back on. Prefer this over remove_keywords.

you want the ad to keep, not just the new ones. The character limits are
checked here first, so a too-long line fails with its own text and length
instead of an opaque API error.

`final_url` exists so a wrong landing page costs an edit rather than the
whole ad. It does NOT excuse guessing: a URL that does not resolve gets
the ad disapproved, so copy it from an already-approved ad in the same
account or confirm the page loads before calling.

Editing an ad sends it back to Google for review and resets its
performance history, so prefer it for fixing copy; to test a new angle,
create a second ad and pause the first.

the current ones.

Changes a keyword's bid, its match type, or both.

The two changes are not alike:

  * A BID change is an in-place update. Raising it needs confirm_spend.
  * A MATCH TYPE change is not possible in place -- Google treats the
    keyword text and match type as the criterion's identity. Changing it
    means removing the keyword and adding it back, which DISCARDS ITS
    HISTORY and gives it a new criterion id, so it needs confirm_remove.

Required when changing the match type, because the
keyword's history is lost.

cpc_bid.description: New max CPC in the account's own currency. Omit to keep.

match_type.description: EXACT, PHRASE or BROAD. Omit to keep.

One line per account: spend, conversions and whether measurement works.

Built for the start of the day. The health check it runs on each account
is the one that matters most and is easiest to miss: an account that
RECORDS conversions but counts none of them towards the Conversions
metric is bidding towards nothing, and every other report in that account
reads as zero.

Accounts are read one at a time and an account that refuses access is
reported rather than failing the whole call -- a deactivated or
unlinked account in the list is normal, not an error.

customer_ids.description:
An explicit list of accounts, instead of discovering
them.

date_range.description: A GAQL literal such as LAST_7_DAYS or THIS_MONTH.

A manager account whose clients to list. Omit to
use every account the credentials can reach.

Gets the account-level settings that silently break measurement.

Four things sit above every campaign and are invisible from campaign
reports: auto-tagging (off means Analytics cannot attribute anything),
call reporting (off means every call extension records nothing), the
conversion attribution window, and the account timezone and currency that
every other number in this server is expressed in.
tools.name: agency_get_account_settings
tools.title: Agency Get Account Settings

tools.description:
Compares month-to-date spend against where it should be by now.

A daily budget is not a monthly cap: Google may spend up to twice the
daily amount on a good day, balancing over the month, so an account can
sit above plan mid-month and still land on target -- or not. This puts
the actual figure next to the straight-line pace so the difference is
visible before the month ends rather than after.

monthly_plan.description:
What the month is supposed to cost, in the account's
own currency. Omit to use the sum of the daily budgets times the
days in the month, which is Google's own implied ceiling.

tools.name: agency_get_budget_pacing
tools.title: Agency Get Budget Pacing

tools.title: Agency List Labels

tools.description:
Reads what this server wrote to an account, newest first.

One entry per write attempt: applied writes, validations, refusals at
the precondition, API failures, and decisions logged by hand with
log_manual_change. Each carries the time in UTC and in Europe/Istanbul,
the tool and its class, the plan id, the operations sent and who asked.

since.description:
Start of the window, "YYYY-MM-DD" or an ISO timestamp.
Defaults to 30 days ago.

until.description: End of the window. Defaults to now.

tools.name: audit_get_change_log
tools.title: Audit Get Change Log

tools.description:
Writes down a change made in the Google Ads interface, and why.

The audit checks compare Google's change history with this log: a
change made in the interface with no entry here is reported as an
undocumented change. Logging it closes that gap. Nothing in the account
is touched.

campaign_id.description: The campaign it concerns, if one.

description.description: What was changed and why, in one or two sentences.

resource_type.description:
What kind of thing, as Google names it in the change
history: CAMPAIGN, AD_GROUP, AD_GROUP_CRITERION, CAMPAIGN_BUDGET,
CAMPAIGN_CRITERION, AD_GROUP_AD, ASSET ...

when.description:
When it was done, "YYYY-MM-DD" or an ISO timestamp. Defaults
to now.

tools.name: audit_log_manual_change
tools.title: Audit Log Manual Change

tools.description:
Runs the full agency checklist against one account.

Same checks, same order, every account -- so "we found this in one
account" becomes "we checked every account". Findings come back
ranked: critical means something is not working or not serving,
warning means money or reach is leaking, note means look and decide.

A check that fails to run is reported in `checks_failed` rather than
failing the audit, because a partial audit is worth more than none.

brand_campaign_ids.description:
Campaigns to leave out of the
PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST check -- a brand campaign may legitimately
want people interested in the area from elsewhere.

lead_contract.description:
What the client pays for: FORM_ONLY, CALLS_ONLY or
FORMS_AND_CALLS. With FORM_ONLY, biddable call goals are
reported; with CALLS_ONLY, biddable form goals are. Omit to
skip that check.

min_wasted_cost.description:
Only report zero-conversion search terms, and
ad groups, that spent at least this much in the last 30 days,
in account currency. Lower it on small accounts.

skip_search_terms.description:
Skip the search-term sweep, which is the
slowest check on a large account.

tools.name: audit_run_account_audit
tools.title: Audit Run Account Audit

tools.description:
Runs the account audit across every account under a manager.

This is the answer to "we fixed that in one account -- is it wrong
in the others too". It runs the same checklist everywhere and then
inverts the result: `shared_findings` lists each finding by how many
accounts have it, so a problem that shows up in three accounts reads
as one job rather than three separate discoveries.

Search terms are skipped by default here; they are the slow check and
the per-account audit is the right place to read them.

An account that cannot be read is listed in `unreachable` rather than
failing the run -- a deactivated or unlinked account is normal.

lead_contracts.description:
Optional map of customer id to FORM_ONLY,
CALLS_ONLY or FORMS_AND_CALLS, for the contract check.

min_wasted_cost.description: Passed through to each account audit.

skip_search_terms.description: Passed through to each account audit.

Creates a Demand Gen campaign. ALWAYS created PAUSED.

Demand Gen runs on YouTube, Discover and Gmail. It looks like Performance
Max from the outside but is NOT built from asset groups -- it keeps ad
groups, and all the creative goes into one multi-asset ad.

Where Performance Max chases conversions across every Google surface,
Demand Gen is the visual, discovery-led one: it wants strong images and
is usually paired with an audience rather than intent signals.

Creates a YouTube video campaign. ALWAYS created PAUSED.

Builds a VIDEO campaign with a responsive video ad. It keeps the
campaign -> ad group -> ad shape, so set_ad_group_status and set_ad_status
work on it as usual.

No channel subtype is set: Google has folded Video Action into Demand Gen
and now rejects the subtype on create.

NOT VERIFIED END TO END. Google returns MUTATE_NOT_ALLOWED for VIDEO
campaign creation on the test account this fork is developed against, and
that could mean either "test accounts cannot do video" or "the API no
longer creates video campaigns at all". The tool translates that error
into an explanation rather than pretending to work. Everything up to the
campaign create -- validation, the video asset, the ad structure -- is
exercised; the create itself is not. Prefer create_demandgen_campaign for
action-focused video until this is confirmed on a production account.

Register the video first with upload_youtube_video_asset, and the logo
with upload_image_asset.

Button text, one of LEARN_MORE, SIGN_UP, SHOP_NOW,
GET_QUOTE, APPLY_NOW, BOOK_NOW, CONTACT_US, SUBSCRIBE, DOWNLOAD,
VISIT_SITE.

long_headlines.description: Long headlines, each at most 90 characters.

target_cpa.description:
Optional target CPA in the account's own currency. Needs
conversion tracking.

video_asset_ids.description: One or more YouTube video asset ids.

Registers an existing YouTube video as an asset.

Nothing is uploaded to YouTube here -- the video must already be public or
unlisted on a channel you control. This only tells Google Ads that the
video exists so a campaign can point at it.

youtube_video_id.description:
The id from the watch URL, e.g. "dQw4w9WgXcQ" from
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ -- the id only, not
the whole URL.

tools.description:
Builds a campaign whose ads exist to make the phone ring.

Call-only ads are gone from the Google Ads API (v25 has no call ad
type), so a "call campaign" is built the way Google now builds one: a
Search campaign, one ad group, a responsive search ad, and a CALL asset
on the campaign so every ad shows the call button and every call is
counted as a conversion. This tool does those steps in order, so the
result is one campaign rather than four half-finished objects.

The campaign is created PAUSED and spends nothing until enable_campaign.
Keywords are optional here so the copy can be reviewed first; add_keywords
fills the ad group afterwards.

bidding_strategy.description:
MANUAL_CPC, MAXIMIZE_CLICKS (default) or
MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS. Conversion-based bidding needs a call
conversion action that actually records.

budget_resource_name.description:
An existing budget, e.g.
"customers/123/campaignBudgets/456". Give this OR daily_budget.

call_conversion_action_id.description:
Count calls against this conversion
action. Omit to use the account's default call action.

country_code.description: Two-letter country of the number, e.g. "TR".

cpc_bid.description:
Max CPC for the ad group, in the account's currency. Used
by MANUAL_CPC only.

daily_budget.description:
Creates a new budget with this daily amount in the
account's own currency. Give this OR budget_resource_name.

final_url.description:
Landing page for the ad, with https://. Copy it from an
approved ad or confirm it resolves; never type it from memory.

headlines.description:
3-15 headlines, at most 30 characters each. Put the
call to action in them ("Hemen Arayın").

keywords.description:
Optional, same shape as add_keywords:
[{"text": "acil çilingir", "match_type": "PHRASE"}].

name.description: Campaign name, unique in the account.

path1.description: Optional display path, at most 15 characters.

phone_number.description: The business number as a local caller would dial it.

tools.title: Campaigns Create Call Campaign

Creates a campaign budget.

A budget on its own never spends; only a campaign that uses it and is
ENABLED can spend. Creating a budget is therefore safe and needs no
confirmation.

customer_id.description: The Google Ads account id. Dashes are fine.

daily_amount.description:
Average daily budget in the ACCOUNT'S OWN currency
(e.g. 500 means 500 TRY in a TRY account). Do not convert to USD.

explicitly_shared.description: True to let several campaigns share this budget.

tools.title: Campaigns Create Campaign Budget

Creates a Search campaign. ALWAYS created PAUSED — it cannot spend.

After this returns, the campaign exists but serves nothing. Add ad groups,
ads and keywords, set geo targeting and a schedule, show the user the whole
plan, and only then call set_campaign_status to enable it.

bidding_strategy.description:
One of MANUAL_CPC, MAXIMIZE_CLICKS,
MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS, TARGET_CPA, TARGET_ROAS.
Note: conversion-based strategies need working conversion tracking;
check that before choosing one.

content_network.description:
Include the Display network. Default False —
leaving this on is a classic way to waste a search budget.

end_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for no end date.

name.description: Campaign name. Must be unique within the account.

start_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today if omitted.

target_cpa.description: Required for TARGET_CPA. In the account's own currency.

target_roas.description: Required for TARGET_ROAS, as a ratio (4.0 means 400%).

tools.title: Campaigns Create Search Campaign

Enables a campaign, which starts real spending.

This is the single gate that lets money move: everything under a
campaign is created ENABLED and stays silent until the campaign itself
is. The refusal carries the daily budget and the implied monthly figure
so the user can be shown real numbers before agreeing.

confirm_spend.description:
Required. Pass True only after showing the user the
daily and implied monthly budget and getting a yes.

tools.name: campaigns_enable_campaign
tools.title: Campaigns Enable Campaign

tools.description:
Looks up language constant ids by name or two-letter code.

Call this before set_campaign_languages -- never guess a language id.
Matching is done here rather than in GAQL because language_constant does
not accept a LIKE filter on every field, and there are few enough
languages to filter in Python.

query.description:
Part of a language name ("Turkish") or its code ("tr").
Omit to list every targetable language.

tools.name: campaigns_find_language_ids
tools.title: Campaigns Find Language Ids

tools.description:
Looks up geo target constant ids for a place name.

Call this before set_campaign_geo_targets — never guess a location id.

country_code.description: Two-letter country code to search within.

tools.name: campaigns_find_location_ids
tools.title: Campaigns Find Location Ids

tools.description:
Pauses a campaign. Stopping spend is always safe, so nothing is asked.

The campaign keeps its history, its ads and its keywords and can be
enabled again with enable_campaign. This is the right first move when
something looks wrong and the cause is not yet known.
tools.name: campaigns_pause_campaign
tools.title: Campaigns Pause Campaign

tools.description:
Sets when a campaign is allowed to serve, in the ACCOUNT'S time zone.

A campaign with no ad schedule runs all week. Once any schedule entry
exists, the campaign serves ONLY inside the entries that exist — so the
schedule you pass must list EVERY block the campaign should run in.

`replace_existing` defaults to True, so this behaves like its name: the
schedule you pass becomes the whole schedule. That matters because a day
is turned OFF by being absent, and an add-only version of this tool
cannot express that at all -- passing Monday-to-Saturday would silently
leave an existing Sunday entry serving.

confirm_spend.description:
Required when the campaign is ENABLED and any block
carries a bid_modifier above 1.0, which raises cost per click
immediately.

replace_existing.description:
True (default) clears the campaign's current ad
schedule first, so the result is exactly what you passed. False
adds to what is already there, which can only widen the hours.

schedule.description:
One dict per time block, e.g.
[{"day": "MONDAY", "start_hour": 9, "end_hour": 23},
 {"day": "TUESDAY", "start_hour": 9, "end_hour": 23,
  "bid_modifier": 0.5}]
Hours are 0-24. Minutes may be 0, 15, 30 or 45 via the optional
"start_minute"/"end_minute" keys; end_hour 24 means midnight.
The optional "bid_modifier" multiplies the bid inside that block:
0.5 bids half, 1.5 bids fifty percent more. Allowed range is
0.1 to 10.0 -- there is no 0, because an hour is turned off by
being absent, not by a modifier. Use a modifier instead of
deleting a block when the hours still convert, only worse: a
deleted block earns nothing and therefore never proves itself
wrong, while a discounted one keeps producing the data the next
decision needs.

tools.name: campaigns_set_campaign_ad_schedule
tools.title: Campaigns Set Campaign Ad Schedule

tools.description:
Sets whether location targeting means presence or mere interest.

Google's default is PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST, which serves the ads to people
merely INTERESTED in the targeted area from anywhere else in the world.
For a business people have to walk into, that is usually the largest
single source of wasted spend, and it is invisible in a campaign report --
only a geo segment shows it.

Narrowing to PRESENCE can only reduce reach, so it needs no confirmation.
Widening back to PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST or SEARCH_INTEREST opens traffic
that was closed, which is the same class of change as removing a negative
keyword, so it requires confirm_widens_reach=True.

confirm_widens_reach.description:
Required when the change opens traffic that
PRESENCE was keeping out.

negative_geo_target_type.description:
How EXCLUDED locations are matched:
PRESENCE or PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST. Omit to keep.

positive_geo_target_type.description:
PRESENCE (people in the area),
PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST (also people interested in it from
elsewhere -- Google's default), or SEARCH_INTEREST.

tools.name: campaigns_set_campaign_geo_target_type
tools.title: Campaigns Set Campaign Geo Target Type

tools.description:
Adds geo targets to a campaign.

Get the ids from find_location_ids first. This ADDS criteria; it does not
replace existing ones. Adding targeting never increases spend beyond the
campaign budget, so no confirmation is needed.

location_ids.description:
Geo target constant ids, e.g. ["2792"] for Turkey,
["1012782"] for Istanbul.

negative.description: True to EXCLUDE these locations instead of targeting them.

tools.name: campaigns_set_campaign_geo_targets
tools.title: Campaigns Set Campaign Geo Targets

tools.description:
Sets which languages a campaign targets.

A campaign created through the API carries NO language criterion, and no
language criterion means ALL languages -- so a Turkish campaign quietly
serves against English-language sessions until this is set. That is not
visible in a campaign report either.

Language targeting matches the user's Google interface language and
recent browsing, NOT the language of the keyword, so this narrows who
sees the ad without touching which queries can match it.

`replace_existing` defaults to True, so this behaves like its name: a
language is turned OFF by being absent, and an add-only version could
not express that.

language_ids.description:
Language constant ids from find_language_ids,
e.g. ["1037"] for Turkish.

replace_existing.description:
True (default) clears the campaign's current
language criteria first. False adds to what is there.

tools.name: campaigns_set_campaign_languages
tools.title: Campaigns Set Campaign Languages

tools.description:
Targets a radius around a point -- the right shape for one shopfront.

District and city targeting are drawn by administration, not by how far
anyone will travel: a district can reach 15km inland while the street two
minutes away sits in the next district and is missed entirely. For a
single-location business a radius around the door matches real catchment.

Layer several radii to bid by distance: call this once per ring with its
own bid_modifier (0-3km at 1.2, 3-6km at 1.0, 6-10km at 0.75). Rings are
separate criteria and Google applies the tightest matching one.

`presence_only` also fixes the setting that quietly wastes local budgets:
Google's default counts people merely INTERESTED in the area, so someone
searching "maltepe berber" from another city still sees the ad. True
restricts to people actually there, which is what a walk-in business
wants.

Give either an address (street_address + city_name, Google geocodes it)
or latitude/longitude. Targeting never spends beyond the campaign budget,
so this needs no confirmation.

bid_modifier.description:
1.2 bids 20% more inside this ring, 0.75 bids 25% less.
Omit for no adjustment.

latitude.description: Use instead of an address, e.g. 40.9412.

longitude.description: Use instead of an address, e.g. 29.1234.

presence_only.description:
True targets people IN the area; False also targets
people merely interested in it. True is right for a shopfront.

radius.description: How far from the point, in radius_units.

replace_existing_locations.description:
True removes the campaign's existing
location and proximity criteria first. Use it when moving from
district targeting to a radius, or the two stack and the wider
one wins.

tools.name: campaigns_set_campaign_proximity
tools.title: Campaigns Set Campaign Proximity

tools.description:
Enables, pauses or removes a campaign. DEPRECATED: prefer the split tools.

Use pause_campaign to stop spend and enable_campaign to start it. This
tool does both, which means a client cannot allow pausing without also
allowing enabling; it stays for one release and then goes.

ENABLED starts real spending and requires confirm_spend=True.
REMOVED is not reversible and requires confirm_remove=True.
PAUSED always works without confirmation -- stopping spend is always safe.

confirm_spend.description:
Required for ENABLED. Pass True only after showing the
user the daily and implied monthly budget and getting a yes.

tools.name: campaigns_set_campaign_status
tools.title: Campaigns Set Campaign Status

tools.description:
Sets the campaign's final URL suffix and/or tracking template.

The final URL suffix is where UTM parameters belong. Google appends it to
the landing page URL after any redirect, so analytics and CRM see the
campaign that produced the click without the ad's own final_url having to
carry the parameters -- which matters because an RSA's final_url cannot
be edited afterwards.

A suffix is per campaign, so a per-campaign utm_campaign value can only
be set here, not at account level.

The tracking template is the redirect mechanism itself and a wrong one
breaks EVERY landing page in the campaign, so it is left alone unless
explicitly passed. Pass an empty string to clear either field.

final_url_suffix.description:
Bare query string with no leading '?', e.g.
"utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=konut-eylul".
ValueTrack parameters such as {keyword} and {adgroupid} are
allowed. Omit to keep; pass "" to clear.

tracking_url_template.description:
Full redirect template, e.g.
"{lpurl}?utm_source=google". Omit to keep; pass "" to clear.

tools.name: campaigns_set_campaign_url_settings
tools.title: Campaigns Set Campaign Url Settings

tools.description:
Bids more or less for an age range or gender, without excluding it.

This is the tool to reach for when data says a group converts better --
not exclude_demographics. A modifier keeps everyone eligible and only
shifts what you pay; an exclusion throws the group away, and on Search
that is usually a mistake because Google does not know most searchers'
age or gender at all. Those unknowns land in AGE_RANGE_UNDETERMINED and
UNDETERMINED, which are typically the largest buckets on the campaign,
so bidding them down is bidding down most of your traffic.

A modifier is a create the first time and an update afterwards; this
tool works out which and does not fail on a second call.

age_ranges.description:
Maps AGE_RANGE_18_24, AGE_RANGE_25_34, AGE_RANGE_35_44,
AGE_RANGE_45_54, AGE_RANGE_55_64, AGE_RANGE_65_UP or
AGE_RANGE_UNDETERMINED to a modifier, 0.1-10.0.

confirm_spend.description:
Required when the campaign is ENABLED and any modifier
is above 1.0.

genders.description:
Maps MALE, FEMALE or UNDETERMINED to a modifier, 0.1-10.0.
1.2 bids 20% more, 0.8 bids 20% less, 1.0 is no change.

tools.name: campaigns_set_demographic_bid_modifiers
tools.title: Campaigns Set Demographic Bid Modifiers

tools.description:
Sets per-device bid adjustments on a campaign.

A modifier multiplies the bid on that device: 1.0 is no change, 1.2 bids
20% more, 0.7 bids 30% less, 0 stops serving on that device entirely.
Raising any modifier above its current value can raise cost per click, so
it requires confirm_spend=True. Lowering is always allowed.

confirm_spend.description: Required when any modifier is being raised.

tools.name: campaigns_set_device_bid_modifiers
tools.title: Campaigns Set Device Bid Modifiers

tools.description:
Bids more or less inside named locations within what is already targeted.

Use this to lean towards the places that actually buy without cutting the
rest loose. Adding a district that sits inside an already-targeted city
does not widen reach -- the city already covered it -- it only makes that
district biddable on its own.

Get the ids from find_location_ids first; never guess one. A location
already on the campaign is updated rather than created, so calling this
twice is safe.

confirm_spend.description:
Required when the campaign is ENABLED and any modifier
is above 1.0.

location_bids.description:
Maps geo target constant ids to modifiers, 0.1-10.0.
For example {"9198902": 1.25} bids 25% more in that district.

tools.name: campaigns_set_location_bid_modifiers
tools.title: Campaigns Set Location Bid Modifiers

tools.description:
Changes a campaign's bidding strategy.

On a PAUSED campaign this is free: it still cannot spend. On an ENABLED
campaign it changes how money is spent right now, so it requires
confirm_spend=True.

Conversion-based strategies (MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS, TARGET_CPA,
TARGET_ROAS) need working conversion tracking in the account. Without it
the API rejects the change with CONVERSION_TRACKING_NOT_ENABLED.

bidding_strategy.description:
MANUAL_CPC, MAXIMIZE_CLICKS, MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS,
TARGET_CPA, TARGET_ROAS or TARGET_IMPRESSION_SHARE.

confirm_spend.description: Required when the campaign is ENABLED.

cpc_bid_ceiling.description:
Maximum CPC, in the account's own currency.
REQUIRED for TARGET_IMPRESSION_SHARE, which bids for position
rather than for a conversion and will otherwise pay whatever the
auction asks -- the usual reason an own-brand campaign costs
several times what a brand click should. Optional for
MAXIMIZE_CLICKS; rejected by the conversion-based strategies.

impression_share_location.description:
Required for TARGET_IMPRESSION_SHARE.
ANYWHERE_ON_PAGE, TOP_OF_PAGE or ABSOLUTE_TOP_OF_PAGE.

impression_share_percent.description:
Required for TARGET_IMPRESSION_SHARE. The
share of auctions to appear in, as a percentage 1-100.

target_cpa.description: Required for TARGET_CPA, in the account's own currency.

target_roas.description: Required for TARGET_ROAS, as a ratio (4.0 means 400%).

tools.name: campaigns_update_bid_strategy
tools.title: Campaigns Update Bid Strategy

tools.description:
Changes a campaign's settings. Status is not changed here.

Use set_campaign_status to enable, pause or remove a campaign; this tool
only touches settings, so it can never start a campaign serving.

Moving the campaign to a LARGER budget raises what it can spend and
requires confirm_spend=True. Everything else here is capped by the budget
that is already in place and needs no confirmation.

budget_resource_name.description:
Move the campaign to a different budget, e.g.
"customers/123/campaignBudgets/456". Omit to keep.

confirm_spend.description: Required only when moving to a larger budget.

content_network.description:
Include the Display network. Omit to keep. Turning
this on for a search campaign is a classic way to waste budget.

name.description: New campaign name. Omit to keep.

search_network.description: Include Google search partners. Omit to keep.

start_date.description:
YYYY-MM-DD. Omit to keep. Cannot be changed once the
campaign has started serving.

tools.name: campaigns_update_campaign
tools.title: Campaigns Update Campaign

tools.description:
Changes a budget's daily amount.

RAISING a budget increases what the account can spend, so it requires
confirm_spend=True. Lowering a budget is allowed without confirmation.

confirm_spend.description:
Must be True when the new amount is higher than the
current one. Only pass True after the user has agreed to that
specific increase.

daily_amount.description: New daily amount, in the account's own currency.

tools.name: campaigns_update_campaign_budget
tools.title: Campaigns Update Campaign Budget

tools.description:
Creates a website conversion action and returns the tag to install.

Creating this costs nothing and changes no bidding on its own. It does
two things: it starts measurement, and it satisfies the precondition for
conversion-based bidding, which the API otherwise refuses with
CONVERSION_TRACKING_NOT_ENABLED.

The returned `tag_snippets` are the actual gtag code. Nothing is measured
until that code is on the site, so pass it to the user -- a conversion
action with no tag installed will report zero conversions forever and
quietly starve any smart bidding strategy pointed at it.

always_use_default_value.description:
True to ignore any value sent by the tag and
always use default_value.

category.description:
What the conversion means. Common ones: SUBMIT_LEAD_FORM,
PURCHASE, SIGNUP, CONTACT, BOOK_APPOINTMENT, REQUEST_QUOTE,
PHONE_CALL_LEAD, QUALIFIED_LEAD, PAGE_VIEW.

click_lookback_days.description:
How many days after a click a conversion still
counts, 1-90. Longer windows suit slow decisions.

counting_type.description:
ONE_PER_CLICK counts one conversion per ad click and is
right for leads. MANY_PER_CLICK counts every one and is right for
sales, where one visitor can legitimately buy twice.

default_value.description:
Value of one conversion, in the ACCOUNT'S OWN currency.
Omit for conversions with no monetary value. Required in practice
for TARGET_ROAS, which has nothing to optimize without it.

name.description: Conversion name, e.g. "Kayit Formu". Unique within the account.

tools.name: conversions_create_conversion_action
tools.title: Conversions Create Conversion Action

tools.description:
Lists the account's conversion actions.

Use this before pointing a campaign at conversion-based bidding: an
account with no ENABLED action, or one whose actions are all excluded
from the conversions metric, has nothing for smart bidding to optimize.

include_removed.description: True to include REMOVED and HIDDEN actions.

tools.name: conversions_list_conversion_actions
tools.title: Conversions List Conversion Actions

tools.description:
Chooses which conversion categories a campaign bids toward.

By default a campaign inherits the account's goals. Setting them here
overrides that for this campaign: the categories you list become biddable
and every other one stops being bid toward, so pass the complete list you
want, not just additions.

On a PAUSED campaign this is free. On an ENABLED campaign it changes what
the bidding is chasing right now, so it requires confirm_spend=True.

biddable_categories.description:
Categories to bid toward, e.g.
["SUBMIT_LEAD_FORM", "PHONE_CALL_LEAD"]. Every other category
present on the campaign is set to non-biddable.

campaign_id.description: The campaign to set goals for.

confirm_spend.description: Required when the campaign is ENABLED.

tools.name: conversions_set_campaign_conversion_goals
tools.title: Conversions Set Campaign Conversion Goals

tools.description:
Changes an existing conversion action, including whether it counts.

This fixes the commonest broken account: an action that records perfectly
but sits OUTSIDE the "Conversions" column, so every conversion-based
bidding strategy in the account is optimizing toward nothing while the
real signal accumulates unused. `include_in_conversions_metric` is that
switch, and it cannot be set at creation time -- only here.

Because that switch decides what smart bidding chases, changing it (or
`primary_for_goal`, or the value) while a conversion-based strategy is
serving requires confirm_spend=True. Renaming is always free.

STATUS CANNOT BE CHANGED HERE. Google's enum has no PAUSED for a
conversion action, and the API refuses HIDDEN and REMOVED on an update.
A conversion action is retired only in the Google Ads interface
(Goals > Conversions > the action > Remove). Passing `status` returns
that explanation instead of an opaque API error.

This does NOT work on GOOGLE_HOSTED actions -- the local actions that
come from the Business Profile, such as "click to call" and "directions".
Google owns those and refuses every mutate with MUTATE_NOT_ALLOWED and
IMMUTABLE_FIELD. To make one of them bid-worthy, make its CATEGORY
biddable on the campaign with set_campaign_conversion_goals instead.

always_use_default_value.description: True to ignore any value sent by the tag.

click_lookback_days.description:
How many days after a click a conversion still
counts, 1-90.

confirm_remove.description: Kept for compatibility; no longer used.

confirm_spend.description:
Required when a change would alter what a serving
conversion-based campaign bids toward.

conversion_action_id.description:
The action to change, from
list_conversion_actions.

default_value.description: Value of one conversion, in the ACCOUNT'S OWN currency.

include_in_conversions_metric.description:
True to feed the "Conversions" column
that smart bidding optimizes; False to keep it for reporting only.

primary_for_goal.description:
True to make this action primary for its goal
category, False for secondary.

status.description:
Not supported -- see above. Any value is refused with the
reason; the parameter stays so older callers get a clear
message rather than a schema error.

tools.name: conversions_update_conversion_action
tools.title: Conversions Update Conversion Action

tools.description:
Uploads the outcome of phone calls that came from ads.

The same restriction as upload_offline_conversions applies: Google
limits ConversionUploadService to accounts already using it, and points
new integrations at the Data Manager API. Check `api_errors` in the
result before believing anything was recorded.

This is how "the call turned into a booking" gets back to Google. It is
keyed on the caller's number and the time the call STARTED, which is what
a call-tracking export gives you, not on a click id.

calls.description:
One dict per call, with keys:
caller_id (required, in E.164, e.g. "+905301234567"),
call_start_date_time (required, with timezone offset),
conversion_date_time (required, with offset),
conversion_value (optional), currency_code (optional).

conversion_action_id.description: An upload-type conversion action for calls.

partial_failure.description: True to accept the valid rows and report the rest.

tools.name: conversions_upload_call_conversions
tools.title: Conversions Upload Call Conversions

tools.description:
Uploads conversions that happened offline, keyed on the Google click id.

CHECK THIS FIRST: Google has closed UploadClickConversions to new
integrations. An account that was not already using it gets
"Usage of ConversionUploadService.UploadClickConversions is limited to
existing users" and nothing is recorded -- the call succeeds, the
conversions do not arrive. New integrations have to go through the
separate Data Manager API, which this server does not speak. The tool
still works for accounts already grandfathered in, and surfaces that
error verbatim in `api_errors` for the rest.

Each entry needs the GCLID that Google put on the landing page URL, the
time the conversion happened, and optionally what it was worth. The
account must have auto-tagging ON or there is no GCLID to key on --
get_account_settings reports that.

Two rules Google enforces and this checks first, because the API's own
error for them is opaque:
  * The conversion time must be AFTER the click. Uploading a booking
    dated before its own click is rejected.
  * conversion_date_time needs an explicit timezone offset, in the form
    "2026-09-01 14:30:00+03:00". A bare timestamp is rejected.

conversion_action_id.description:
The conversion action to attribute these to. It
must be of an upload type; create_conversion_action makes one.

conversions.description:
One dict per conversion, with keys:
gclid (required, or gbraid / wbraid for app and iOS traffic),
conversion_date_time (required, with offset),
conversion_value (optional number),
currency_code (optional, defaults to the account's),
order_id (optional, dedupes re-uploads).

partial_failure.description:
True to accept the valid rows and report the bad
ones, instead of rejecting the whole batch. Usually what you
want for a spreadsheet export.

tools.name: conversions_upload_offline_conversions
tools.title: Conversions Upload Offline Conversions

tools.description:
Returns ids of customers directly accessible by the user authenticating the call.

Use this tool first to discover available customer IDs if the user hasn't
provided one. Most other tools require a valid customer ID as input.

Returns:
    List[str]: A list of customer IDs.
tools.name: customers_list_accessible_customers
tools.title: Customers List Accessible Customers

tools.description:
Creates a campaign experiment in SETUP, without starting it.

Nothing is live and nothing is spent until schedule_experiment is called,
which is deliberate: the treatment campaign that Google generates is what
you edit, and it does not exist until then.

A 50/50 split reaches significance soonest. Splits below about 20% take
so long on a small account that the test finishes after the decision was
needed.

base_campaign_id.description:
The live campaign to test against. It keeps running
as the control.

days.description:
How long to run. Under 14 days rarely settles on a small
account.

description.description: Optional note on what the treatment will change.

name.description: What is being tested, e.g. "tCPA 150 vs Maximize Conversions".

traffic_split.description:
Percentage of traffic sent to the TREATMENT arm,
1-99. The control gets the rest.

tools.name: experiments_create_experiment
tools.title: Experiments Create Experiment

tools.description:
Ends a running experiment, discarding the treatment campaign.

The treatment's traffic returns to the base campaign. Use graduate to
keep the treatment instead.

confirm.description: Required. The treatment campaign and its learning are lost.

tools.name: experiments_end_experiment
tools.title: Experiments End Experiment

tools.description:
Promotes the treatment arm into a permanent campaign of its own.

Graduating gives the treatment campaign its own budget and takes it out
of the experiment, so it becomes a normal campaign running alongside the
base one. That is a real spend increase: the treatment no longer shares
the base campaign's budget, it has its own.

campaign_budget_id.description:
The budget the graduated campaign will use.
create_campaign_budget makes one.

confirm_spend.description:
Required. The graduated campaign spends its own
budget on top of the base campaign's.

experiment_id.description: The experiment whose treatment should survive.

tools.name: experiments_graduate_experiment
tools.title: Experiments Graduate Experiment

tools.description:
Lists the account's campaign experiments and their arms.

Status is what matters: SETUP means it was created but never scheduled,
so it is testing nothing. That is the usual way an experiment gets
forgotten.
tools.name: experiments_list_experiments
tools.title: Experiments List Experiments

tools.description:
Deletes an experiment.

Meant for the experiments that never ran: a SETUP experiment created by
mistake, or one superseded before it started. Deleting a RUNNING
experiment throws away its treatment campaign and every measurement it
has collected -- end_experiment or graduate_experiment are the deliberate
ways to finish one of those.
tools.name: experiments_remove_experiment
tools.title: Experiments Remove Experiment

tools.description:
Starts a SETUP experiment and creates its treatment campaign.

From this point the treatment arm serves real ads to a real share of the
base campaign's traffic. It does not add budget -- the split divides what
the base campaign already spends -- but it does change what that money
buys, so it needs confirmation.

confirm_spend.description: Required. The treatment arm begins serving.

tools.name: experiments_schedule_experiment
tools.title: Experiments Schedule Experiment

tools.description:
Adds a call extension, and with it the only biddable measure of calls.

For a local business this is usually the highest-value extension there
is: it puts a call button on the ad, and -- unlike the "click to call"
action that comes from the Business Profile -- the calls it produces
become a NORMAL conversion action that smart bidding can actually bid
toward. Google-hosted local actions cannot; they are immutable and the
API refuses to make them biddable.

Measurement rides on a Google forwarding number, which Google swaps in
for the real one so it can time the call. That needs call reporting
switched on at account level -- this tool reads that setting back and
says so when it is off, because with it off the extension still shows
but nothing is measured.

Extensions cannot raise spend beyond the campaign budget, so this needs
no confirmation.

call_conversion_action_id.description:
Count calls against THIS conversion action
instead of the account default. Omit to use the account default,
which is what most accounts want.

campaign_id.description: The campaign to add the call button to.

country_code.description: Two-letter country of the number, e.g. "TR".

disable_call_conversion.description:
True to show the button but measure nothing.
Only for an account that already tracks calls another way.

phone_number.description:
The business number as a local caller would dial it,
e.g. "0530 407 49 50". Spaces and dashes are stripped.

replace_existing.description:
A campaign with a call extension already gets the
existing one back untouched, since a second one is duplication,
not safety. True removes the old link first.

tools.name: extensions_add_call_extension
tools.title: Extensions Add Call Extension

tools.description:
Adds callout extensions to a campaign.

Callouts are short, non-clickable selling points shown under the ad
("Ucretsiz Deneme Dersi", "7/24 Destek"). Google needs at least two and
shows up to six. They are the cheapest extension to write and the least
risky, because nothing links anywhere.

callouts.description: Callout texts, each at most 25 characters.

campaign_id.description: The campaign to add them to.

tools.name: extensions_add_callout_extensions
tools.title: Extensions Add Callout Extensions

tools.description:
Adds sitelink extensions to a campaign.

Sitelinks are extra links under the ad, each to a different page. Google
generally needs at least FOUR before it will show them, and it picks which
to show, so give it a real set rather than one.

Extensions cannot raise spend beyond the campaign budget, so this needs no
confirmation.

campaign_id.description: The campaign to add them to.

sitelinks.description:
One dict per sitelink, e.g.
[{"text": "Ucretsiz Deneme", "url": "https://site.com/deneme",
  "description1": "Ilk ders bizden",
  "description2": "Hemen kayit ol"}]
"text" is at most 25 characters, the two descriptions 35 each and
are optional -- but supply both or neither, Google ignores a lone
one.

tools.name: extensions_add_sitelinks
tools.title: Extensions Add Sitelinks

tools.description:
Adds a structured snippet extension to a campaign.

A structured snippet is a header plus a list, shown as "Courses: YKS, TYT,
AYT". The header is NOT free text -- Google only accepts its own list, and
the values must actually be instances of it.

campaign_id.description: The campaign to add it to.

header.description:
One of Google's headers, e.g. "Courses", "Degree programs",
"Service catalog", "Types", "Brands", "Styles", "Amenities",
"Destinations", "Insurance coverage", "Models", "Neighborhoods",
"Shows", "Featured hotels".

tools.name: extensions_add_structured_snippets
tools.title: Extensions Add Structured Snippets

tools.description:
Attaches a location asset set to a campaign, so its ads show an address.

Adding an extension does not raise the bid or the budget; it makes the ad
bigger and more specific, which usually raises click-through rate. On a
local account it also filters: someone who sees the address and the
distance and still clicks is closer to walking in.

campaign_id.description: The campaign that should show the address.

tools.name: extensions_attach_location_asset_set
tools.title: Extensions Attach Location Asset Set

tools.description:
Lists the extensions linked to a campaign, as flat records.

Covers sitelinks, callouts, structured snippets, call and promotion
assets. Each row is the extension's own content plus its asset_id and
status -- not the raw proto, which is mostly unset fields. Address
extensions are NOT here: they come from an asset set synced from
Business Profile, which list_location_asset_sets reports.

Check this before adding: extensions are assets that get LINKED, so
running add_sitelinks twice does not update the first set, it creates a
second one and the campaign ends up with duplicates competing for the
same slot.
tools.name: extensions_list_campaign_extensions
tools.title: Extensions List Campaign Extensions

tools.description:
Lists the location asset sets Google synced from Business Profile.

If this comes back empty, no Google Business Profile is linked to the
account and no campaign can show an address. That link is made in the
Google Ads interface, not through the API, and it is worth checking on
every local-business account: an address extension is one of the few
things that both raises click-through rate and pre-qualifies the click
by showing how far away the shop is.
tools.name: extensions_list_location_asset_sets
tools.title: Extensions List Location Asset Sets

tools.description:
Unlinks an extension from a campaign.

This removes the LINK, not the asset: the asset stays in the account and
can be linked again, so this is recoverable. It still needs confirmation
because the ad loses that extension immediately.

campaign_id.description: The campaign to remove it from.

confirm_remove.description: Must be True. Say which extension is going first.

tools.name: extensions_remove_campaign_extension
tools.title: Extensions Remove Campaign Extension

tools.description:
Repoints an existing call extension at a conversion action, in place.

The common broken state, and the reason this exists: an extension left on
USE_RESOURCE_LEVEL_CALL_CONVERSION_ACTION with no action actually set.
The button shows, people call, and the call lands nowhere. Removing and
re-creating the asset would fix it too, but that detaches the extension's
history -- so change the field instead.

Pass exactly one of use_account_default, call_conversion_action_id or
disable_call_conversion.

asset_id.description: The call asset to fix, from list_campaign_extensions.

use_account_default.description:
Count calls against the account's own call
conversion action. This is the right answer for most accounts,
and the fix for the empty-resource-level state above.

tools.name: extensions_update_call_extension
tools.title: Extensions Update Call Extension

tools.description:
Gets volume and bid data for keywords you already have in mind.

Unlike research_keywords this suggests nothing -- it answers "what are
these specific terms worth?" for a list you already wrote, which is the
check to run before add_keywords rather than after.

keywords.description: The exact terms to look up.

language_id.description: Language constant id. 1037 is Turkish, 1000 English.

location_ids.description: Geo target constant ids from find_location_ids.

tools.name: keyword_research_get_keyword_historical_metrics
tools.title: Keyword Research Get Keyword Historical Metrics

tools.description:
Finds keyword ideas with real search volume, competition and bid ranges.

Give seed keywords, a page URL, or both -- Google mines the page for terms
when a URL is supplied, which usually beats guessing seeds by hand.

Volumes are monthly averages for the locations and language requested, so
the location matters: researching Turkish terms against the default US
geo returns numbers that describe the wrong market. Pass location_ids from
find_location_ids.

keywords.description: Up to 20 seed terms, e.g. ["yks kursu", "tyt hazirlik"].

language_id.description: Language constant id. 1037 is Turkish, 1000 English.

limit.description: Maximum ideas to return, ordered by monthly searches.

location_ids.description:
Geo target constant ids from find_location_ids, e.g.
["21069"] for Istanbul. Omit to let Google use the account default.

network.description:
GOOGLE_SEARCH, or GOOGLE_SEARCH_AND_PARTNERS for a wider and
usually more optimistic estimate.

page_url.description:
A page to mine for ideas, e.g. "https://mdkampus.com/yks".
Google mines its own index, so a page it has not crawled returns
an empty list rather than an error -- an empty result means "no
ideas for this page", not "the call failed".

tools.name: keyword_research_research_keywords
tools.title: Keyword Research Research Keywords

tools.description:
Retrieves the selectable, filterable, and sortable fields for a specific Google Ads resource,
including compatible metrics and segments.

Use this tool to find out which fields you can select, filter by, or sort by
when querying a specific resource (e.g., 'campaign', 'ad_group').
This tool also returns metrics and segments that can be selected with the resource.
Their names start with 'metrics.' and 'segments.' respectively.

Do not guess fields, you MUST use this tool to discover them before constructing a query for the
`search` tool.

The responses of this tool should be cached, as they don't change frequently.

resource_name.description: The name of the Google Ads resource (e.g., 'campaign', 'ad_group').

tools.name: metadata_get_resource_metadata
tools.title: Metadata Get Resource Metadata

tools.description:
Writes out the Turkish forms a negative keyword needs to cover.

For a term it returns the locative (-de/-da/-te/-ta), the locative
relative (-deki/-daki), the possessive locative (-inde/-ında, -sında
after a vowel), the plural (-ler/-lar), and every one of those typed
without Turkish letters (ü -> u, ş -> s, ı -> i ...). Negatives never
match close variants, so each form is a separate negative to Google.

On a multi-word term only the last word is inflected. It adds nothing
anywhere: pick the forms that apply and pass them to
add_to_negative_keyword_list.

term.description: The word or phrase, e.g. "ücretsiz kurs".

tools.name: negatives_expand_turkish
tools.title: Negatives Expand Turkish

tools.description:
Applies a plan produced by a SPEND or DESTRUCTIVE tool.

Before writing, every object the plan read is read again and compared
with the plan's "before". If anything differs, the write is refused and
the plan is marked stale: make a new one. After writing, the tool's own
read-back is returned as `actual`, next to what the plan `requested`.

A plan applies exactly once. A DESTRUCTIVE plan (something is removed
or detached) also needs confirm_destructive=True, given only after the
user has been told what is lost.

With GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_REQUIRE_DRY_RUN=true the first apply of a plan is
a validation only and the second one writes.

plan_id.description: From the plan returned by the tool.

validate_only.description:
True to have Google validate the request without
writing anything. Repeatable; does not consume the plan.

tools.name: plans_apply_plan
tools.title: Plans Apply Plan

tools.name: plans_discard_plan
tools.title: Plans Discard Plan

tools.description: Shows a plan: its changes, impact, limits verdict, rollback and status.
tools.name: plans_get_plan
tools.title: Plans Get Plan

tools.description: Lists open plans, newest first.

customer_id.description: Limit to one account. Omit for every account.

include_finished.description:
True to also list applied, stale, failed,
expired and discarded plans (kept for seven days).

tools.name: plans_list_plans
tools.title: Plans List Plans

tools.description:
Adds an audience signal to a Performance Max asset group.

An audience signal tells Google who to start with; like a search theme it
is a hint, not a restriction, and Performance Max will reach beyond it.
It cannot raise spend, so it needs no confirmation.

The audience must already exist in the account. This server does not
create audiences.

asset_group_id.description: The asset group to add the signal to.

tools.name: pmax_add_pmax_audience_signal
tools.title: Pmax Add Pmax Audience Signal

tools.description:
Adds search themes to a Performance Max asset group.

Search themes are hints, not keywords: Google treats them as a starting
point for what people might search, and will still serve outside them.
They cannot be negated and they do not cap anything, so they never raise
spend and need no confirmation.

asset_group_id.description: The asset group to add them to.

themes.description:
Phrases, each at most 80 characters, e.g.
["yks hazirlik kursu", "istanbul ozel ders"].

tools.name: pmax_add_pmax_search_themes
tools.title: Pmax Add Pmax Search Themes

tools.description:
Creates a Performance Max campaign. ALWAYS created PAUSED.

Builds the campaign, one asset group, and the links between the asset
group and the assets you pass -- upload images first with
upload_image_asset, or find existing ones with discover_existing_assets.

Performance Max only bids toward conversions, so the account needs a
conversion action before this will work. Omit both targets for plain
Maximize Conversions; give target_cpa or target_roas to add a target.

Unlike a Search campaign there are no keywords here, and no individual ads
to pause: Google assembles ads from these assets and decides where they
run. What steers it is the asset set plus the signals you add afterwards
with add_pmax_search_themes and add_pmax_audience_signal.

asset_group_name.description:
Name for the asset group. Defaults to the campaign
name.

business_name.description: The advertiser's name, at most 25 characters.

descriptions.description:
2-5 descriptions, at most 90 characters -- the FIRST is
limited to 60, because Google uses it where space is tightest.

logo_asset_ids.description: At least one logo id, square.

long_headlines.description: 1-5 long headlines, each at most 90 characters.

marketing_image_asset_ids.description: At least one landscape (1.91:1) image id.

name.description: Campaign name. Must be unique within the account.

square_image_asset_ids.description: At least one square (1:1) image id.

target_cpa.description: Optional target CPA, in the account's own currency.

target_roas.description: Optional target ROAS as a ratio (4.0 means 400%).

tools.name: pmax_create_pmax_campaign
tools.title: Pmax Create Pmax Campaign

tools.description:
Lists assets already in the account, so they can be reused.

Check this before uploading: assets are account-level and reusable, and
uploading the same logo for every campaign clutters the account without
making anything work better.

asset_type.description:
Filter by type, e.g. IMAGE, TEXT, YOUTUBE_VIDEO. Omit for
all types.

tools.name: pmax_discover_existing_assets
tools.title: Pmax Discover Existing Assets

tools.description: Lists an asset group's audience signals.
tools.name: pmax_get_pmax_audience_signals
tools.title: Pmax Get Pmax Audience Signals

tools.description: Lists an asset group's search themes.
tools.name: pmax_get_pmax_search_themes
tools.title: Pmax Get Pmax Search Themes

tools.description:
Removes a search theme or audience signal from an asset group.

Covers both signal kinds: the resource is the same, only its payload
differs. Removing a signal changes who Google starts with, so it takes
confirmation even though nothing is destroyed permanently -- the signal
can be added back.

asset_group_id.description: The asset group to remove the signal from.

confirm_remove.description: Must be True. Name the signal going first.

criterion_id.description:
The signal's id, from get_pmax_search_themes or
get_pmax_audience_signals.

tools.name: pmax_remove_pmax_signal
tools.title: Pmax Remove Pmax Signal

tools.description:
Uploads an image so it can be used in a Performance Max asset group.

Give a URL to fetch, or the bytes directly as base64. The image lives at
account level and can be reused by any asset group, so upload once and
pass the id around rather than uploading the same file per campaign.

Google's minimums, which it enforces on use rather than on upload:
landscape marketing images at least 600x314, square images and logos at
least 128x128 (300x300 recommended), under 5 MB.

image_url.description: URL to fetch the image from. Give this or image_base64.

name.description: A name for the asset. Must be unique within the account.

tools.name: pmax_upload_image_asset
tools.title: Pmax Upload Image Asset

tools.description:
Gets per-ad metrics with ad strength and whether the ad may serve at all.

An ad with no impressions is ambiguous until you know its approval status:
a DISAPPROVED ad and a merely unlucky one look identical in a metrics-only
report. This returns both, and lists the disapproved ads separately so
they cannot be missed.
tools.name: reports_get_ad_performance
tools.title: Reports Get Ad Performance

tools.description:
Gets campaign metrics for a period.

Costs come back in the ACCOUNT'S OWN currency, already out of micros. CTR
is a percentage. cost_per_conversion and roas are null when there is
nothing to divide by, rather than zero, so an untracked campaign is not
mistaken for a free one.

campaign_id.description: Limit to one campaign. Omit for all of them.

date_range.description:
LAST_30_DAYS, LAST_7_DAYS, THIS_MONTH, LAST_MONTH,
YESTERDAY, TODAY and the other GAQL literals, or an explicit
"YYYY-MM-DD,YYYY-MM-DD" pair.

tools.name: reports_get_campaign_performance
tools.title: Reports Get Campaign Performance

tools.description:
Gets the campaign -> ad group -> ads/keywords hierarchy.

Use this to orient before changing anything: it returns the ids the write
tools need, so a plan can be built without guessing at structure.

campaign_id.description: Limit to one campaign. Omit for all of them.

tools.name: reports_get_campaign_structure
tools.title: Reports Get Campaign Structure

tools.description:
Gets who changed what in the account, and when.

The first question to ask when performance moves without an obvious cause.
It also exposes changes nobody on the team made: Google's auto-apply
subscription edits live accounts under the user_email
"Recommendations Auto-Apply", and removing a negative keyword that way
can reopen spend on traffic somebody deliberately shut off.

Google keeps roughly 30 days of change history and caps the query at
10,000 rows; the range must be given as change_event dates, which this
handles.

date_range.description:
A GAQL literal or "YYYY-MM-DD,YYYY-MM-DD". Beyond about
30 days the API returns nothing.

limit.description: Maximum rows, at most 10000. Newest first.

tools.name: reports_get_change_history
tools.title: Reports Get Change History

tools.description:
Breaks conversions down by conversion action, and says which ones count.

Google keeps two totals. `conversions` is only the actions whose
include_in_conversions_metric is on -- the number every Smart Bidding
strategy optimises against. `all_conversions` is everything recorded. An
account can record hundreds of real leads and still report zero
conversions, and then Maximize Conversions is bidding towards an event
that never happens.

This is the first call to make on an inherited account, before reading any
other performance number.

campaign_id.description: Limit to one campaign. Omit for the whole account.

tools.name: reports_get_conversion_performance
tools.title: Reports Get Conversion Performance

tools.description:
Gets how much of the available auction the ads actually appeared in.

This is the one report that separates "we cannot afford more" from "we are
not good enough to win more":

  * budget_lost -- the auction was entered and lost to our own daily cap.
    Raising the budget buys these impressions directly.
  * rank_lost -- lost on Ad Rank: bid, quality score or extensions.
    Raising the budget buys nothing here.

Shares are percentages. They are only reported for Search campaigns and
are withheld by Google when the sample is too small, in which case the
field is null rather than zero.

campaign_id.description: Limit to one campaign. Omit for all of them.

tools.name: reports_get_impression_share
tools.title: Reports Get Impression Share

tools.description:
Gets per-keyword metrics with the quality score components.

The overall quality score is a 1-10 summary; the three components say
which part is weak, and each has a different fix:

  * expected_ctr below average -- the keyword does not match the intent,
    or the ad does not answer the query.
  * ad_relevance below average -- the ad copy does not use the query's own
    words. Rewrite the ad, not the keyword.
  * landing_page below average -- the page does not deliver what the ad
    promised. No bid change fixes this.

Quality score is only populated for keywords with enough traffic; it comes
back as null otherwise, which is not the same as a low score.
tools.name: reports_get_keyword_performance
tools.title: Reports Get Keyword Performance

tools.description:
Splits performance by device, time, network, geography or date.

The write tools can already set device bid modifiers and an ad schedule.
This is what tells you WHICH modifier to set: without it those settings
are guesses.

campaign_id.description: Limit to one campaign. Omit for the whole account.

segment.description:
One of device, day_of_week, hour, day_hour, geo, network,
date.

tools.name: reports_get_performance_by_segment
tools.title: Reports Get Performance By Segment

tools.description:
Gets the real searches that triggered the ads.

This is what people actually typed, as opposed to the keywords bid on.
It is the raw material for negative keywords: anything here that should
never have matched is a candidate for add_negative_keywords.

campaign_id.description: Limit to one campaign. Omit for all of them.

min_impressions.description: Skip terms below this, to cut the long tail.

tools.name: reports_get_search_terms
tools.title: Reports Get Search Terms

tools.description:
Finds spend that produced no conversions, as data to judge.

Deliberately named `get_`, not `analyze_`: it returns the rows and draws
no conclusion. Zero conversions is not automatically waste -- a term can
be new, seasonal, or assisting a conversion credited elsewhere -- so the
decision belongs to whoever can see that context, not to this tool.

Two lists come back. Search terms are the usual fix, via
add_negative_keywords. Keywords are the slower one: pause or lower the
bid rather than remove, so the history survives.

campaign_id.description: Limit to one campaign. Omit for all of them.

min_cost.description:
Ignore anything that cost less than this, in the account's
own currency.

tools.name: reports_get_wasted_spend
tools.title: Reports Get Wasted Spend

tools.description:
Lists the account's campaigns with their settings.

No metrics here, so no date range and no cost: this is the "what exists"
call. Use get_campaign_performance for the numbers.
tools.name: reports_list_campaigns
tools.title: Reports List Campaigns

tools.description:
Lists Google's own recommendations, and the account optimisation score.

Read this; do not apply it blindly. Several recommendation types exist to
grow Google's inventory rather than the advertiser's result --
SEARCH_PARTNERS_OPT_IN and DISPLAY_EXPANSION_OPT_IN both widen where the
ads run, which for a tightly-targeted local account is usually spend
leaving the target audience. Others, such as
RESPONSIVE_SEARCH_AD_IMPROVE_AD_STRENGTH or adding a missing extension,
are worth acting on.

Optimisation score is Google's own metric and is NOT a performance
measure: an account can score 100% while converting nothing.

include_dismissed.description: True to also list ones already dismissed.

tools.name: reports_list_recommendations
tools.title: Reports List Recommendations

tools.description: Fetches data from the Google Ads API using the search method

conditions.description: List of conditions to filter the data, combined using AND clauses

limit.description: The maximum number of rows to return

resource.description: The resource to return fields from

tools.name: search_search
tools.title: Search Search

tools.description:
Adds negative keywords to an existing shared list.

Terms already in the list are skipped rather than duplicated, so this is
safe to call repeatedly with an overlapping batch.

Negatives never match close variants, so a Turkish list needs both the
accented and the unaccented spelling of a word to block both.
tools.name: shared_sets_add_to_negative_keyword_list
tools.title: Shared Sets Add To Negative Keyword List

tools.description:
Attaches a shared negative keyword list to one or more campaigns.

This is the step that makes the list do anything. Attaching narrows what
a campaign can match, so it can only reduce spend, never increase it --
but it can silence traffic somebody wanted, so read the list's terms
first with get_negative_keyword_list_terms.
tools.name: shared_sets_attach_negative_keyword_list
tools.title: Shared Sets Attach Negative Keyword List

tools.description:
Creates a shared negative keyword list, optionally with its first terms.

Creating a list spends nothing and blocks nothing until it is attached to
a campaign with attach_negative_keyword_list. That second step is the one
people forget.

match_type.description:
EXACT, PHRASE or BROAD for those terms. BROAD blocks any
query containing all the words -- the usual choice for a
one-word exclusion. Negatives never match close variants, so
spelling and accents must be listed explicitly.

name.description:
A name that says what the list excludes, e.g.
"Free and DIY" or "Competitor names". Must be unique.

tools.name: shared_sets_create_negative_keyword_list
tools.title: Shared Sets Create Negative Keyword List

tools.description:
Detaches a shared negative keyword list from a campaign.

Detaching REOPENS every query the list was blocking, which is a spend
increase, so it needs confirmation.

campaign_id.description: The campaign to remove it from.

confirm.description: Required, because this widens what the campaign can match.

tools.name: shared_sets_detach_negative_keyword_list
tools.title: Shared Sets Detach Negative Keyword List

tools.description: Gets the terms inside one shared negative keyword list.
tools.name: shared_sets_get_negative_keyword_list_terms
tools.title: Shared Sets Get Negative Keyword List Terms

tools.description:
Lists the account's shared negative keyword lists.

Read this before creating a new one: accounts accumulate near-duplicate
lists, and a list attached to nothing is a common and invisible failure.
tools.name: shared_sets_list_negative_keyword_lists
tools.title: Shared Sets List Negative Keyword Lists

tools.description:
Deletes a shared negative keyword list entirely.

Removing a list that is still attached to campaigns REOPENS every term
it was blocking on all of them at once, so the count of attached
campaigns is named in the confirmation rather than left for the caller
to look up.

confirm_remove.description: Required. The list and its terms are gone for good.

tools.name: shared_sets_remove_negative_keyword_list
tools.title: Shared Sets Remove Negative Keyword List

tools.description:
Removes individual terms from a shared negative keyword list.

Before this existed, fixing one wrong term meant rebuilding the whole
list. Now a term is removed by its text (any match type, or one given
match type) or by its criterion id from get_negative_keyword_list_terms.

Removing a negative REOPENS the searches it was blocking on every
campaign the list is attached to, which is a spend increase, so this is
a removal and needs confirmation. Terms that are not in the list are
reported, not treated as an error.

confirm_remove.description: Must be True. Say which searches will match again.

criterion_ids.description: Criterion ids to remove, as an alternative.

keywords.description: Term texts to remove. Matching ignores case.

match_type.description:
EXACT, PHRASE or BROAD to remove only that match type
of the given texts. Omit to remove every match type.

tools.name: shared_sets_remove_terms
tools.title: Shared Sets Remove Terms

tools.description:
Adds audiences to a Search campaign, in observation or targeting mode.

OBSERVATION changes nothing about who sees the ads; it starts collecting
performance per audience and lets a bid modifier apply. TARGETING
restricts the campaign to these audiences only, which on Search usually
collapses volume -- so it needs confirm_reach_cut.

A bid modifier of 1.2 bids 20% more for people in the audience; 0.8 bids
20% less. Setting one before there is data is guessing.

audience_ids.description: Ids from the newer combined `audience` resource.

campaign_id.description: The campaign to add them to.

user_list_ids.description:
Remarketing / customer-match list ids, from
list_audiences.

tools.name: targeting_add_audience_to_campaign
tools.title: Targeting Add Audience To Campaign

tools.description:
Excludes age ranges or genders from a campaign.

Use this only where the exclusion is a fact about the service, not a
guess about who buys: a men's barber excluding nothing is usually right,
because a woman booking for her son is a real customer. Excluding
AGE_RANGE_UNDETERMINED is almost always a mistake -- it is the largest
single bucket on Search, since Google does not know most searchers' age.

age_ranges.description:
Any of AGE_RANGE_18_24, AGE_RANGE_25_34, AGE_RANGE_35_44,
AGE_RANGE_45_54, AGE_RANGE_55_64, AGE_RANGE_65_UP,
AGE_RANGE_UNDETERMINED.

tools.name: targeting_exclude_demographics
tools.title: Targeting Exclude Demographics

tools.description:
Lists the audience segments this account can target or observe.

Includes the account's own remarketing lists, whose size matters: Google
requires roughly 1,000 active visitors before a Search remarketing list
can serve, and a list below that is listed here but will never match.
tools.name: targeting_list_audiences
tools.title: Targeting List Audiences

tools.description:
Lists everything a campaign targets or excludes, grouped by kind.

Locations, audiences, demographics, languages, devices and negative
criteria all live in the same campaign_criterion table, which is why they
are easy to lose track of. This groups them and states whether audiences
are in observation or targeting mode, and what
positive_geo_target_type is -- PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST there is the
commonest silent leak on a local account.
tools.name: targeting_list_campaign_targeting
tools.title: Targeting List Campaign Targeting

tools.description:
Removes campaign criteria: audiences, demographic exclusions, and so on.

This is the inverse of add_audience_to_campaign and
exclude_demographics. Removing a NEGATIVE criterion widens what the
campaign can reach and therefore what it can spend, which is why that
case is gated; removing a positive one narrows it and is not.

Criterion ids come from list_campaign_targeting.

confirm_widens_reach.description: Required when any of them is an exclusion.

tools.name: targeting_remove_campaign_criteria
tools.title: Targeting Remove Campaign Criteria
